specs.anchorText: A model train set photographed at the right angle is indistinguishable from a real railway
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a one-eyed cartoon camera character (a friendly camera with a single lens for an eye, looking confident) photographing two scenes through identical viewfinder frames. On the left, a tiny tabletop model railway with a miniature train; on the right, a full-size real railway with a real train. Inside the camera's viewfinder both scenes look exactly identical, shown as one shared framed picture between them. A small confident sparkle near the camera's lens suggests it cannot tell them apart. Gentle humor, soft palette, clean white background, generous margins, like a friendly science-textbook cartoon. No text or lettering in the image. Keep it simple and focused on the single idea that scale is invisible to one lens.
specs.alt: A one-eyed cartoon camera photographs a tiny model train set and a real full-size railway, and both produce an identical framed image, illustrating the depth-scale ambiguity that makes a single image unable to recover absolute scale, the trick behind miniature special effects.
specs.caption: A single lens gives you shape for free but scale never: a dollhouse and a real house can land identical pixels, which is exactly how miniature effects fool the eye on purpose.

specs.anchorText: A point cloud is a swarm of fireflies that agree on nothing.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: three friendly workbench stations side by side, each building the same little rabbit shape a different way. Left station: a swarm of tiny glowing dots loosely forming a rabbit, like fireflies (a point cloud). Middle station: the same rabbit built from stacked cubic blocks inside a large mostly-empty cube frame, with many empty cells visible (a voxel grid). Right station: the same rabbit folded from flat triangular panels like origami (a triangle mesh). A small friendly robot stands at each station admiring its version. Soft palette, clean white background, generous margins, approachable textbook-cartoon style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep it simple, three clear stations, one shared shape.
specs.alt: Three workbench stations each build the same rabbit a different way: a swarm of glowing dots as a point cloud, stacked cubes inside a mostly-empty cube frame as a voxel grid, and folded triangular panels as a mesh, illustrating the three explicit 3D representations and their differing memory and surface trade-offs.
specs.caption: The same geometry, three ways to write it down: a point cloud of fireflies that agree on nothing, a city of mostly-empty voxel blocks, and origami that took a graphics PhD to fold.

specs.anchorText: Max-pooling runs the world's most ruthless meeting.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a big crowd of identical small cartoon points (little round characters), each holding up a tiny speech bubble shouting an opinion. A friendly robot moderator wearing a referee whistle stands at a podium and, for each topic, keeps only the single loudest character (drawn glowing and standing tall) while the rest sit quietly with dimmed bubbles. The few chosen loud characters together faintly outline the silhouette of a chair, suggesting the critical points that summarize the shape. Gentle, inclusive humor, soft palette, clean white background, generous margins, XKCD-meets-children's-science-book style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition focused on one idea: only the loudest voice per feature survives.
specs.alt: A robot moderator at a podium keeps only the single loudest shouting point-character for each topic while dimming the rest, and the chosen loud characters faintly outline a chair, illustrating how PointNet's symmetric max-pool selects a sparse set of critical points to give an order-independent global descriptor.
specs.caption: A symmetric max-pool runs the most ruthless meeting in machine learning: for each feature it keeps only the loudest point, and that tiny clique of critical points is enough to still recognize the chair.

specs.anchorText: A NeRF is the most non-committal way to store a scene ever invented.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly small neural-network character (a little glowing brain-box with a polite shrug) sitting in the middle of an empty room. The furniture of the room (a sofa, a lamp) is invisible except exactly where a thin glowing ray from a tiny cartoon camera strikes it, lighting up that one spot into solid color while the rest of the object stays as faint dotted outlines. Several rays touch different points, each illuminating only its hit point. The network character looks calm and a little smug, as if saying it will only answer when asked. Soft palette, clean white background, generous margins, gentle and approachable textbook-cartoon style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the single idea clear: geometry appears only where a ray queries it.
specs.alt: A small smug neural-network character sits in a room whose sofa and lamp are faint dotted outlines, solid in color only where thin glowing camera rays strike them, illustrating that a NeRF stores the scene implicitly in its weights and reveals geometry only when queried along a ray.
specs.caption: A NeRF is a five-megabyte promise: the room has no fixed mesh or coordinates and exists only as a standing willingness to tell you the color of any point the moment you point a ray at it.

specs.anchorText: Seurat spent two years dabbing tiny dots onto one canvas
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly robot painter wearing a beret, joyfully flinging a few handfuls of soft translucent colored ellipsoid blobs (like pastel marshmallows) at a canvas all at once. Up close near the robot the blobs look like a fuzzy cloud of overlapping ovals; toward the far side of the canvas the same blobs visibly fuse into a crisp little picture of a cathedral. A small speed clock or motion lines suggest it happens fast. Gentle humor, soft palette, clean white background, generous margins, approachable textbook-cartoon style reminiscent of pointillism. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the single idea clear: many translucent blobs blend into a sharp image, instantly.
specs.alt: A robot painter in a beret flings handfuls of soft translucent colored ellipsoid blobs at a canvas, where up close they look like a fuzzy cloud of overlapping ovals but resolve into a crisp cathedral toward the far side, illustrating how 3D Gaussian splatting blends millions of anisotropic blobs into a photorealistic real-time image.
specs.caption: Splatting is pointillism at three hundred frames per second: step too close and the cathedral dissolves into a haze of translucent marshmallows, step back and it snaps into a photograph.

specs.anchorText: When two of your photos insist a surface is both beige
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: two cartoon photographs of the same wall pinned up side by side, one tinted slightly more beige than the other, each with a small confused arrow pointing at the wall. Between them, a polite cartoon optimizer character (a friendly robot in a tiny bow tie, calm like a helpful clerk) is conjuring a faint semi-transparent ghost blob floating in mid-air that looks beige from one photo's side and slightly-more-beige from the other's. The robot looks composed and pleased, as if it found a clever loophole rather than made a mistake. Gentle, inclusive humor, soft palette, clean white background, generous margins, approachable textbook-cartoon style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the single idea clear: contradictory photos make the optimizer invent a floating ghost.
specs.alt: Two slightly different-colored photos of the same wall flank a calm bow-tied optimizer robot that conjures a faint semi-transparent floating ghost blob looking correct from each photo, illustrating how NeRF and splatting invent floater geometry when captures disagree because the photometric loss faithfully fits inconsistent data.
specs.caption: A floater is the optimizer honestly answering a dishonest question: when two photos disagree about a surface, it calmly conjures a semi-transparent ghost that satisfies both, so the cure is better captures, not more training.
